title: Tech Note: Keeping the Memory Clean - Part 1

historical_commentary.text: This is Part 1 of a two-part series (companion to asset 11778, Part 2) explaining how 4D uses memory and offering tips for optimizing memory usage in databases and forms; as with Part 2, the specific memory-management concerns described are tied to the limited-RAM constraints of classic Mac OS/Windows 3.1/95 systems of the era, making the concrete guidance obsolete relative to modern hardware and 4D's evolved memory handling, though the general discipline of memory-conscious application design remains a timeless principle.
related_updates: Modern computers have vastly more RAM and modern 4D versions include substantially improved automatic memory management compared to the constrained classic Mac OS/Windows 3.1/95 environments this note addresses
Specific 1997-era form/database memory-optimization tips are no longer necessary or applicable given decades of evolution in both 4D's internal memory handling and underlying OS memory management
